rationale: Format-preserving encryption returns a value of the same shape, so a nine-digit value stays nine digits and downstream systems that validate the field still accept it.

The exact ciphertext is asserted as well as the properties. FF3-1 is specified in NIST SP 800-38G Rev 1, so the ciphertext is determined by the key, tweak, radix and plaintext, not by the implementation. Two implementations that disagree here cannot re-identify each other's output, which breaks the reversibility the encrypting strategies exist to provide. phileas uses io.github.mysto:ff3 with the key and tweak given in this case's policy.
Verified byte-identical across separate processes, so this is a stable expectation rather than a snapshot of one run.
A hyphenated value keeps its hyphens in the same positions, so only the digits are encrypted.
This is the case that fails if an implementation strips punctuation before encrypting and does not put it back.
The exact ciphertext is asserted alongside the properties, so a divergence in FF3 parameters is caught rather than passing silently.
